series: Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, Reason #23 (the guessed deadline)
hook: Your goal didn't fail. Your deadline was a guess.

gate.goal_link: a goal with an optimistic date looks 'failed' halfway, so people quit a goal that was on a normal pace
gate.mechanism: planning fallacy: estimates come from the best-case scenario and ignore how long similar past tasks took; Buehler, Griffin & Ross 1994: students predicted ~34 days for their thesis, actual ~56 (real figures 33.9 / 55.5). Fix = the outside view (reference class: your own past project)

frame.want: a design portfolio to switch careers
frame.obstacle: 4-week guess, half done at week 4, feels behind and stops
frame.cost: a goal dropped at 50% that was on a normal pace
frame.fix: before setting a date, ask how long the last similar thing took you; plan that (6 weeks before -> plans 9)
